principles.text: Gap risk caps size, not the stop: positions stay at 20-25% of the account even when a tight stop (MSTR ~0.75%) would allow 35-40%, because nothing else limits an after-hours gap loss.

Sizing history: before 2026 ~25-30% positions (rarely 35%) at 0.5% risk; in 2026 lowered to 20-25% at ~0.3% risk to shrink drawdowns in the chop - 'an optimisation for my style: low win rate, tight risk'.
Slippage is not sized for explicitly, but it is one reason he will not size up just because the stop is tight.
Avoid long entries on gap-up days: the gap stretches price >1% from the EMAs, so even a gentle pullback stops a tight-stop entry whose price is far from support.
After repeated stop-outs in leaders, stop buying into strength and wait for a proper pullback entry (memory leaders into the daily 9, IGV/software pullback alerts set before the open).

A strong bounce that takes out the prior high and all the EMAs is uncommon in a genuinely weak market; when it happens and a short stops out at the open, cover correlated shorts too (gold with silver) - it is not the time for that short.
A selective tape - some names in a group follow through, others in the same group fade - means no easy group-wide move; be pickier and smaller.

Risk management is 'the holy grail'; a trader who doesn't blow up but doesn't grow should study his trades for the upside leak: sizing too small, hesitating when the market is good, or booking small gains too early.
